subject: Recap + Fast-start plan: Concurrency SLO gating for AcmeAI
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@acmeai.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Performance discovery call (concurrency / burst behavior)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed fast-start plan so we’re aligned before engineering digs in:

Highlights from call:
- Target p95 latency for your interactive flows: <= 200ms at 6KB avg sequence length.
- Sustained throughput goal: 120 reqs/s across the service during business hours.
- Target concurrency per model: expected spikes to 350 concurrent in 30s bursts during reporting windows.
- Streaming requirement: partial token flush every 40ms for UI streaming (frontend needs sub-50ms frame updates).

Primary risks we flagged:
- Cold-start scale-up must be <30s to avoid user-visible queues.
- Large spikes (x8 baseline) may require warm capacity or a staged model fallback to smaller quantized variant.
- Queueing behavior: you prefer hard SLO gating vs queue growth — need to decide acceptable tail latency vs request rejection.

Proposed fast-start plan (next 2 weeks):
1) Redwood runs a short lab run using your anonymized load profile (attach acme-load-profile.csv) to measure scale-up times and streaming cadence.
2) Ben will produce a one-page runbook for a warm-pool configuration + SLO gating rules (attach draft runbook).
3) Neha to propose a canary schedule (traffic %, duration) and fallback variant mapping (full -> quant8 -> micro).
4) Joint meeting to lock on acceptance criteria: p95 <=200ms for core path, max scale-up 30s, and streaming frame <=50ms.

Can you confirm: (a) permission to run the lab with the attached load profile, (b) whether rejection at high queue depth is acceptable as an initial gating strategy, or would you prefer always-serve with degraded model?

Thanks — I’ll attach the runbook draft and a sample KPI dashboard after Ben and Neha comment.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir@acmeai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Performance discovery call (concurrency / burst behavior)

Thanks Rachel — all good summary. Quick answers:

- You have permission to use the attached anonymized load profile for lab runs.
- For initial rollouts we prefer hard gating (reject) when queue depth exceeds threshold; critical SLA users should see failures rather than large tail latencies.
- The streaming cadence requirement is firm for the customer-facing product; partial token flush every ~40ms is required.

A couple clarifications for the run:
- Average token length is closer to 450 tokens / 6.5KB; there is a 10% long-tail at ~2.5x that.
- Our current infra has a warm pool of tiny instances but they take ~70s to reach full model-ready state — we’d like Redwood’s recommendation if warm pool can be shorter.

Elena will own the canary approvals; I’ve looped her in.

Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform, AcmeAI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@acmeai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Performance discovery call (concurrency / burst behavior)

Samir / Rachel / Neha —

Attaching a concise "fast-start" runbook and the test matrix we propose. TL;DR of what Redwood will test in the lab:
- Warm-pool config: pre-warm 50% of peak concurrency using lightweight warm instances (KV cache + model half-loaded) to target scale-up <20s.
- Scale-up strategy: staged autoscale — first add warmed workers (20s), then spin full workers (additional 10-20s) to hit long tail.
- Queueing & gating: implement a soft queue with strict max-depth => enforce rejection at depth 250 (configurable) and emit rejection metric + alert.
- Fallback mapping: full_fp16 -> quant8_4x -> micro-quant (reduced context) with automatic QoS tagging.

Attached items: redwood-fast-start-runbook-v1.pdf, acme-load-profile.csv (sanitized). Please review runbook page 2 for the exact test matrix (throughput targets, target p95, streaming validation steps).

Action items:
- Samir: confirm sample of long-tail traffic for week-of testing.
- Neha: schedule the lab and canary plan; propose specific canary windows.
- Rachel: I'll join the kickoff and provide internal run results within 48 hours of test completion.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment stubs ---
redwood-fast-start-runbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
acme-load-profile.csv (text/csv)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>, Samir Khan <samir@acmeai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + Fast-start plan: Concurrency SLO gating for AcmeAI

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Samir. I’ve scheduled the lab run for Oct 19 09:00–12:00 PT and the canary template for Oct 21 02:00–06:00 PT (low-traffic window per your notes). Items I will validate during the lab:
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency under controlled scaled bursts across the three model tiers.
- Streaming flush cadence: instrumented spikes and verification of <50ms partial token window.
- Scale-up times from zero and from 50% warm-pool levels.
- Rejection behaviour: ensure rejected requests return a consistent error code + rate-limited backlog metric.

I will share the test harness link and live dashboard 24 hours before the run: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-runbooks

If that window looks good, we’ll proceed; Ben and I will capture results and a short decision matrix for whether to increase warm-pool, lower rejection depth, or enable staged fallback.

Best —
Neha Kapoor
Senior SRE Solutions, Redwood Inference
